So, the day on the same date for an ordinary year will be 1 day ahead and the day on the same date for a leap year will be 2 days ahead for the next year.

If 11 August 1918 is Sunday, then the day on these dates will be:

11 August 1919 → Monday

11 August 1920 → Wednesday

11 August 1921 → Thursday

11 August 1922 → Friday

11 August 1923 → Saturday

11 August 1924 → Monday

11 August 1925 → Tuesday

Number of days between 11 August 1925 to 4 December 1925 = (20 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 4) = 115

115 when divided by 7, leaves 3 as remainder.

Tuesday + 3 = Friday

Therefore, it will be Friday on 4 December 1925.

Hence, ‘**Friday**’ is the correct answer.

So, 4 December 1925 = Sunday + 5 + Friday.

questions.question: In Cricket, if the umpire extends both hands horizontally it means __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**wide ball.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wide ball:-**

 
 
• **When the umpire extends both hands horizontally in cricket, it means that the ball has been declared a wide ball.**
 
• A wide ball is a delivery that is bowled** outside the batsman's reach and is not able to be hit by the batsman.**
 
• The umpire extends both hands horizontally to signal a wide ball to the **scorers and the players on the field.**
 
• This signal is recognized universally across all** cricket-playing nations.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Dead ball:-**

 
 
• It is a ball that is not in play and cannot be hit by the batsman.
 
• It is usually declared by the umpire in case of an injury or when the ball gets stuck in the equipment of a fielder.
 
 
 
• ** No-ball:-**
 
 
• It​** **is a delivery that is bowled illegally, for instance, if the bowler oversteps the crease while bowling or if the delivery is above waist height.
 
• A no-ball results in the batting team getting an extra run and an additional ball to face.
 
 
 
• ** Run out:-**
 
 
• It **i**s a mode of dismissal in cricket when a batsman is out of his crease and a fielder throws the ball onto the stumps before the batsman can return to his crease.
 
• This can happen when the batsmen attempt to take a run or when the ball hits the bat and deflects onto the stumps.

questions.question: Since complete equality is impossible, the _____ of the Indian Constitution deals with the right to equality and equal protection of law subject to appropriate classification.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** अनुच्छेद 14.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Constitution's emphasis on equality is related to Article 14, which guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the law to all persons within the territory of India.
 
• Article 14
 
 
• Article 14 of the Indian Constitution is about 'Equality Before Law' and it states:
 
• "The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India."
 
• This article is a fundamental right under Part III of the Constitution of India, which talks about Rights to Equality.
 
• The principle of 'Equality before law' is of British origin, while 'Equal protection of the laws' is borrowed from the Constitution of the United States.
 
 
 
• 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 

 
 

 **Article 15**
 
 
Article 15 prohibits discrimination by the state against any citizen on grounds only of caste, religion, sex, race, and place of birth.

 
Fundamental rights are provided to every citizen of the country without any discrimination.

 
These rights entitle an individual to live life with dignity.

 
 
 

 **Article 16**
 
 
Article 16 of the Indian Constitution guarantees equal opportunity to all citizens in matters related to employment in the public sector.

 
The provision of equality is only applicable to the employment or offices which are held by the State.

 
The State is still free to lay down the requisite qualifications for the recruitment of employees for the Government services.

 
 
 

 **Article 13**
 
 
 
• Article 13 deals with Laws Inconsistent with Fundamental Rights.
 
• Article 13 declares that all laws that are inconsistent with or in derogation of any of the fundamental rights shall be void.
 
• It expressively provides for the doctrine of judicial review.
 
• This power has been conferred on the Supreme Court (Article 32) and the high courts (Article 226) that can declare a law unconstitutional and invalid on the ground of contravention of any of the Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: Following are the industry categories classified under the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956, EXCEPT:

options.text: industries with public sector taking the lead and the private sector playing a supplementary role
industries with exclusive ownership of the state

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution 1956:-**

 
 
• **It was a policy framework for the development of industries in India.**
 
• The policy classified industries into three categories: (1) industries in the private sector, (2) industries with the public sector taking the lead and the private sector playing a supplementary role, and (3) industries with exclusive ownership of the state.
 
• The** policy did not include industries in the cooperative sector** as a separate category.
 
• The cooperative sector refers to businesses that are owned and operated by **a group of individuals who share the profits and control the operations.**
 
• ** The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 was replaced by the New Industrial Policy in 1991, which encouraged liberalization, privatization, and globalization of industries in India.**
 
• **Highlights of IPR 1956:**
 
 
• In order to initiate a new industry or expand existing capacity, private entrepreneurs were supposed to obtain licenses from the government.
 
• Licensing, imposition of the tax, tax exemptions, and subsidies were used by the government:
 
 
• to regulate private industries.
 
• bring about a reduction in regional disparities in industrial development. 
 
• to keep a check on the production of goods that are socially undesirable.
 
 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industries with public sector taking the lead and the private sector playing a supplementary role:-**

 
 
• It refers to industries where the government takes the lead in ownership and management, and the private sector plays a supportive role.
 
• This model was adopted for industries such as steel, coal, and power generation.
 
 
 
• **Industries in the private sector:-**
 
 
• It refers to industries that are owned and operated by private individuals or companies. This model was encouraged for industries such as consumer goods, textiles, and services.
 
 
 
• **Industries with exclusive ownership of the state:-**
 
 
• It refers to industries that are wholly owned and operated by the state. This model was adopted for industries such as defense, atomic energy, and railways.

questions.question: Pola festival is associated with which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Maharashtra.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Pola Festival

 
 
• Pola Festival is a thanksgiving festival celebrated by farmers in Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh, to acknowledge the importance of bulls and oxen, who are a crucial part of agriculture and farming activities.
 
• It falls on the day of the Pithori Amavasya in the month of Shraavana.
 
• The farmers decorate their bulls on this day and then worship them to perform in the festival.
 
• This festival is celebrated to show their gratitude towards the bulls for their assistance in the agricultural works by the farmers.
 
• On the following day of the festival, the plowing activities are started and seeds are sown in the fields.

__
 
• The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2011 gave constitutional status and protection to cooperative societies.
 
• In this context, it made the following three changes in the Constitution:
 
 
• It made the right to form cooperative societies a fundamental right (Article 19).
 
• It included a new Directive Principle of State Policy on the promotion of cooperative societies (Article 43-B).
 
• It added a new Part IX-B in the Constitution which is entitled “The Cooperative Societies” (Articles 243-ZH to 243-ZT).
 
 
 
• The new Part IX-B contains various provisions to ensure that the cooperative societies in the country function in a democratic, professional, autonomous, and economically sound manner.
 
• It empowers the Parliament in respect of multi-state cooperative societies and the state legislatures in respect of other cooperative societies to make the appropriate law.
 
• Article 43B deals with the promotion of cooperative societies. The State shall endeavor to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management of co-operative societies. [Article 43B Inserted by the 97th Constitution Amendment Act, 2011].

• It is enshrined in Article 19(c) of the Constitution, which guarantees the freedom to form associations or unions.

• Article 19(1)(c) guarantees all citizens the right "to form associations or unions or co-operative societies".
